test_case.test_name: Parameterized IOMMU-enabled AMD driver per-BDF binding validation
test_case.purpose: Verify the approved IOMMU-enabled configuration is active through firmware, boot and runtime layers and amdgpu binds every expected GPU without IOMMU/DMA/driver/PCIe/xGMI error.
required_package: Approved BIOS IOMMU policy and kernel command-line/runtime mode oracle
Eight-GPU stable BDF/device-ID/topology and expected IOMMU domain/group map
Approved configuration/reboot window, OOB access and rollback procedure
Expected module/version/link/health and error acceptance criteria
test_case.test_command: Capture current firmware policy, cmdline and per-BDF state; apply only the approved IOMMU-enabled configuration and reboot if separately authorized. After boot, prove the exact cmdline, kernel IOMMU enable/translation state and expected domains/groups, then verify loaded amdgpu version and binding/PCIe/health for every expected BDF with complete logs.
test_case.expected_result: The approved IOMMU-enabled mode is active rather than merely requested, every expected GPU is in the intended domain/group and bound to amdgpu, and no IOMMU fault, DMA error, XID, PCIe/xGMI or BMC error appears.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires consistent firmware, cmdline and runtime IOMMU evidence plus complete per-BDF binding/health. A token, module-loaded flag or truncated grep alone cannot pass.
safety_gate: BIOS/cmdline changes and reboot require explicit approval with OOB and rollback.
Do not change unrelated firmware options or use all/random BIOS modification.
Inventory active GPU workloads/services before any driver or boot change.
Abort on boot/access loss, unexpected IOMMU mode/domain, missing BDF, binding failure or DMA/IOMMU fault; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant ID and separate duplicate-row identity
Approved BIOS/cmdline target and pre/post boot identity
test_case.recovery: On boot or binding failure, preserve bootloader, kernel, domain, BDF and logs, then use only the approved OOB rollback to the prior BIOS/cmdline configuration. Do not cycle settings or retry automatically.
